explanations.text:
●  the shape is named                                  ([the shape](skeleton))
  │     The skeleton tells a file as the file's own
  │     structure: one line per part, plain words in
  │     the slots where code stands.
  │     It wins when the user thinks in that structure.
  │
  ●  the rules bind the telling                          ([the rules](Rules))
  │     The structure leads and the parts stand
  │     indented under their holder.
  │     An open slot gets filled with what that part
  │     of the code does.
  │     The pins are block pins, so the skeleton
  │     carries the real lines itself.
  │
  ●  one example shows it whole                      ([the example](Example))
        The hello world server, told as its own skeleton.
        The abstraction above it keeps the user's words
        and points down into it.
